stem.en: Magnesium has 12 electrons. Calcium has 20. Both sit in the second column. What do they have in common?

text.en: Both have two valence electrons. Magnesium's shells are 2, 8, 2 and calcium's are 2, 8, 8, 2.
Both have 12 electrons in their outer shell.

feedback.en: No shell in these atoms holds twelve. Magnesium's twelve electrons are spread over three shells, with just two on the outside.

text.en: Both have the same number of shells.

feedback.en: Magnesium has three shells, calcium has four. Same column means same outer count, not same size. Going down a column, atoms get bigger.
Magnesium is one of the lightest metals there is. The column has nothing to do with weight.

explanation.en: Subtract the full inner shells. Magnesium: 12 minus 2 minus 8 leaves 2. Calcium: 20 minus 2 minus 8 minus 8 leaves 2.
